column3: Direct parallel: other gods are adopted in expectation of protection and aid.
Acquiring monumental works for permanence is only a distant analogue to seeking honor through a constructed support.
Directly rejects the false elevation of Jesus and Mary to gods besides Allah.
Direct challenge to wanting gods apart from Allah.
Immediate sequel: the supposed gods will deny their worship and become opponents.
Directly asks whether honor is sought from a false ally, then locates all honor with Allah.
Adopted gods of supposed nearness vanish when their help is needed.
Continues the local account of disbelievers being driven onward, without developing the false-support claim itself.
Generic statement that an act is not difficult for Allah.
Adopted gods lack creative power and control over benefit, harm, death, life, and resurrection.
Completes the aid expectation: the alleged gods cannot help their worshippers.
Shows an inward desire being installed as a god, though honor is not the stated motive.
Challenges whether alleged gods can protect their followers when they cannot even help themselves.
Local continuation of judgment, with no distinct account of false gods or honor.
Divine might and wisdom here concern prophetic warning, not acquired honor or rival worship.
Taking Satan as an enemy does not illuminate taking gods for honor.
Prohibits another god alongside Allah and states the resulting blame and abandonment.
Affirms Allah's exclusive sovereignty and might while rejecting association with Him.
Treating signs and messengers as mockery is a different misuse of taking.
The blamed and banished outcome loosely parallels failed worldly aspiration, but lacks the rival-god premise.
Exclusive divinity supplies the theological ground, though the verse does not address honor-seeking.
Denies any protectors who can help apart from Allah.
Shows attachment to false gods as a loyalty people resist abandoning.
Political satisfaction over avoiding misfortune is unrelated to worship or honor.
Mocking warning signs concerns rejection, not seeking honor through substitute gods.
Mockery of the messenger does not address the focus relation.
Allah's might is affirmed, but no rival support or honor-seeking is in view.
Denies a protector or intercessor besides Allah at the point of accountability.
Taking desire as a god supplies an alternative form of misplaced allegiance.
Challenges the fantasy that any force besides the Merciful can provide rescue.
Taking Abraham's station as a place of prayer is unrelated to taking gods for honor.
The command to strive with the Quran has no material connection.
States that one whom Allah leaves astray has no guiding protector.
Prophetic communication and divine guidance do not address the focus.
Forbids taking any trustee besides Allah, a positive counterpoint to substituting supports.
Explicitly denies both protector and helper besides Allah.
Generic statement of Allah's power.
Opening address to disbelievers alone adds no relevant claim.
Mocking signs is unrelated to rival worship as a source of honor.
Exact corrective: whoever seeks honor must recognize that all honor belongs to Allah.
Calls for worship and obedience of Allah, the proper allegiance contrasting with false worship.
Satan's claim over a share of servants does not develop the focus.
Challenges whether earth-derived gods can raise the dead, testing their claimed divine capacity.
Call to seek forgiveness is not a neighbor for the focus claim.
Generic affirmation of Allah as the best judge.
Directly rebukes a people for taking gods besides Allah without clear authority.
Noah's persistent call has no specific relevance.
Affirms Allah as the God of humankind, supporting exclusive worship without the honor motive.
Those taking protectors besides Allah remain under Allah's guardianship, not their chosen supports.
Exclusive one-God confession is foundational but does not address the claimed benefit of false gods.
Questions the adoption of powerless, unreasoning intercessors besides Allah.
Commands taking the one God as trustee, the proper alternative to substitute protectors.
Those associated with gods besides Allah are led to the path of Hell, showing the end of that allegiance.
Misplaced intimate friendship is only an indirect analogue to relying on a false ally.
Using oaths as a shield is unrelated to gods or honor.
The calf episode shows a false idol adopted despite clear signs.
Directly denies that any gods besides the Merciful were appointed for worship.
Ethical treatment of guests does not address the focus.
Direct challenge to producing proof for gods taken besides Allah.
The calf was adopted during Moses' absence, an early concrete case of false worship.
Jonah's restoration to righteousness is unrelated to false supports.
Direct affirmation that the worshipped God is one.
Taking devils as protectors besides Allah explains a different form of mistaken reliance.
Exclusive divinity and resurrection authority provide only broad theological support.
Admission into mercy of the righteous has no relevant connection.
Directly rejects the existence of any god other than Allah and condemns association.
Asks whether the beings invoked besides Allah can help their worshippers or themselves.
Allah's sole dominion is followed by denial of any protector or helper besides Him.
Those facing punishment find no helpers besides Allah, exposing failed reliance.
The use of desire in a sexual context does not concern worship or honor.
Denies that anyone besides Allah can remove the approaching event, a broader false-support parallel.
Those called besides Allah possess not even the smallest share of dominion.
Direct parable of people taking protectors besides Allah: their shelter is inherently fragile.
Shows communal insistence on retaining named gods despite their eventual failure to help.
Direct case of taking religious authorities and the Messiah as lords besides Allah.
Rejects attributing a child to Allah, but not the focus's adoption of external gods for honor.
Forbids taking disbelievers as protectors, a social-support parallel rather than idol worship.
Military preparedness does not bear on false worship or honor.
Explicitly denies the condemned any protectors besides Allah.
Direct prohibition of calling upon another god alongside Allah.
Critiques worship without authority or knowledge and denies wrongdoers any helper.
Allah's strength and might support the theme only at a general level.
Challenges alleged partners to show any creative share or revealed warrant.
Affirms one God in heaven and earth, excluding divided divine jurisdiction.
Those worshipped besides Allah cannot provide provision or exercise power.
Divine strength in establishing justice is not about rival gods or honor-seeking.
Rejects taking an inner ally apart from Allah, His messenger, and believers.
The calf's adopters receive humiliation, the direct reversal of seeking honor through an idol.
Alleged beings besides Allah have no ownership, partnership, or supporting role in creation.
Affirms Allah's strength and might without directly treating substitute worship.
Making a past people an example does not connect to the focus.
Allah has no child, partner, or helper born of weakness; His greatness excludes dependent supports.
The exposure of evil deeds and mockery is not specific to false gods or honor.
Direct prohibition against calling on anyone alongside Allah in places of worship.
Misuse of scripture for worldly gain does not address the focus relation.
Abandoning the Quran is a different use of taking.
The closing identification of whisperers has no material connection.
Directly forbids setting another god alongside Allah.
Exclusive prayer to Allah in danger indirectly exposes the insufficiency of rival attachments.
The Quran's inviolability is unrelated to taking gods for honor.
Direct prohibition against setting up equals to Allah despite knowing His sole provision and creation.
Directly tests worship besides Allah by the alleged object's inability to harm or benefit.
Challenges calling on beings besides Allah that cannot benefit or harm and would reverse guidance.
At judgment, claimed intercessors and partners are absent, leaving the worshippers alone.
Those invoked besides Allah are servants who cannot answer or act.
The alleged beings besides Allah cannot help their callers or themselves.
Names the intercessor claim made for beings worshipped besides Allah and rejects its warrant.
Forbids invoking what neither benefits nor harms apart from Allah.
False gods called besides Allah do not avail their worshippers when divine judgment arrives.
Those invoked besides Allah cannot answer; their supplication is portrayed as futile.
Beings invoked besides Allah create nothing, are created, and lack life or awareness.
Alleged beings besides Allah cannot remove or redirect harm.
The very beings invoked seek nearness, mercy, and protection from Allah themselves.
Claimed partners are summoned at judgment but give no response or rescue.
Invoked beings besides Allah cannot create even a fly or recover what it takes from them.
Invoking another god without proof is condemned as a claim for which one is accountable to Allah.
Directly condemns worship of what cannot benefit or harm besides Allah.
Challenges whether any alleged partners create, provide, cause death, or give life.
The invoked cannot hear or answer, and on Judgment Day will repudiate their association.
Rejects taking gods besides Allah whose intercession cannot help when harm is intended.
States the explicit motive of taking protectors besides Allah: supposed nearness to Him.
Challenges whether beings invoked besides Allah can remove harm or withhold mercy.
Contrasts taking protectors besides Allah with Allah alone as the true Protector who gives life.
Those invoked besides Allah possess no intercession except by truthful witness and knowledge.
Challenges claimed partners besides Allah to show creation, a share in creation, or revealed authority.
Calls invocation of beings besides Allah that never answer the furthest form of error.
At the gathering, invoked beings become enemies and reject their worship, closely paralleling 19:82.
Describes taking equals besides Allah as a competing object of devoted allegiance.
The messenger is forbidden from worshipping the beings people invoke besides Allah.
On the Day of Gathering, worshippers and their claimed partners are separated for judgment.
The claimed partners disclaim awareness of the worship directed to them.
Attributes the setting up of rivals to Allah to a misdirecting religious allegiance.
When alleged partners are confronted, they repudiate the worshippers' false claim.
Precedes 26:93 by demanding the location of the beings they had worshipped.
At judgment, Allah calls for the claimed partners whom people asserted.
The claimed partners are summoned but cannot answer their callers or avert punishment.
Idols worshipped besides Allah cannot provide provision, so provision and worship belong with Allah.
No intercessors arise from the alleged partners, and their partnership is disavowed.
Angels repudiate being the worshippers' protectors and identify the actual false allegiance.
Judgment confronts people with the entities they used to associate beside Allah.
The associated beings are lost from their worshippers, exposing their earlier invocation as falsehood.
Explains that named objects worshipped besides Allah have no revealed authority and that judgment belongs only to Him.
Argues that multiple gods in heaven and earth would corrupt their order, affirming Allah's exclusive sovereignty.
Defines Allah as the True and whatever is invoked besides Him as false.
Forbids invoking any other god alongside Allah and attaches grave accountability to doing so.
Again identifies Allah as the True and what is invoked besides Him as false.
